operations.specification: Handles user account registration for the TodoList application. Creates a new user record with provided email and password. The operation corresponds to the todo_list_user Prisma model and is the fundamental entry point for user authentication.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new user by creating a record in the todo_list_user table. The email field is required and must be unique as defined by the unique index on the todo_list_user table. The password_hash field is populated with a BCrypt-hashed value derived from the user's input password, never storing plain-text credentials. The created_at and updated_at fields are automatically set to the current timestamp with no user-provided values allowed. This operation enables users to establish their identity in the TodoList application and will be used to generate the initial JWT tokens for subsequent authentication.

The implementation strictly follows the todo_list_user schema where email must be a valid, unique string and password_hash is a non-nullable string field. There are no other authentication fields available in the schema, so extensions like email verification or two-factor authentication cannot be implemented. This operation is public and requires no prior authentication.

The user identity established here is the sole basis for all subsequent operations in the TodoList application. Each task created, viewed, updated, or deleted will be bound to this user record through the id field. No other actor types exist in this application.

Security considerations are addressed through BCrypt hashing and the exclusion of any sensitive fields beyond email and password_hash in the request body. The system does not implement password recovery, reset, or change functions as these fields are not present in the todo_list_user schema. The created_at field provides auditability of account creation time.

This join operation must be executed before any login or refresh operations. It is the foundational authentication step. The generated response body will contain the JWT tokens necessary for subsequent API calls.
operations.summary: Registers a new user account in the TodoList application.

requestBody.description: Contains the email and password for a new user account.

responseBody.description: Returns JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated access to TodoList application.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticates an existing user by validating their email and password against the todo_list_user table. Provides JWT tokens for subsequent API access. This is the core authentication mechanism for member-level users.
operations.description:
This operation authenticates a user by validating their provided email and password against the stored credentials in the todo_list_user table. The email field is matched against the unique index, and the password_hash field is compared using BCrypt hashing logic derived from the input password. This operation assumes the todo_list_user table contains valid, non-nullable email and password_hash fields as defined in the schema.

When successful, this operation returns a JWT access token and refresh token that establish a secure session. The user's identity is bound to the id field from the todo_list_user record, which will be used in all subsequent protected operations. No other authentication mechanisms are implemented as the schema does not contain fields for email verification, password reset, or two-factor authentication.

The login operation serves as the primary point of entry for authenticated users to access their TodoList data. It must be called after user registration (join) and before any protected operations. The operation only accepts email/password as credentials and rejects all other authentication methods due to schema limitations.

Security is maintained through the use of BCrypt hashing (as implemented in the todo_list_user schema) and short-lived access tokens. The lack of additional auth fields like last_login_at or login_attempts prevents implementation of account lockout or brute force protection.

This operation is the critical gateway to protected resources in the TodoList application. The system is designed exclusively around member users, so this operation serves all users regardless of role.
operations.summary: Authenticates a user and issues JWT access and refresh tokens.

requestBody.description: Contains email and password for authentication.

responseBody.description: Returns JWT access and refresh tokens for authenticated API access.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Refreshes the expired access token using a valid refresh token. Maintains user session without requiring password re-entry. This operation leverages the refresh token mechanism established during login and join operations.
operations.description:
This operation exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token, allowing users to maintain their session without re-entering their password. The refresh token must have been issued during a previous join or login operation and must still be valid according to its expiration policy.

The implementation relies on the session management system created during authentication but does not require any specific database fields beyond the existence of a refresh token table (which would be separate from todo_list_user schema). The todo_list_user schema validates that email and password_hash exist for initial authentication, but refresh token storage is handled separately in an external session management system.

The refresh operation enables continuous access to protected resources without compromising security through long-lived access tokens. After successful refresh, a new access token is issued and the previous refresh token may be invalidated based on security policy.

The refresh mechanism is designed to work in conjunction with the login operation and should be used when access tokens expire. No database fields in the todo_list_user schema are involved in this refresh process, as the refresh token is managed outside the primary user table.

This operation must follow successful login or join operations and enables a seamless user experience by avoiding the need to re-authenticate with credentials repeatedly.
operations.summary: Refreshes the user's access token using a valid refresh token.

requestBody.description: Contains the refresh token to be exchanged for a new access token.

responseBody.description: Returns a new JWT access token for continued authenticated access.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a specific user account by userId for administrative viewing purposes. It queries the todo_list_user table using the provided user ID, returning a single user record. The operation is designed for admin users to view user details for support or audit purposes. No sensitive authentication fields like password_hash are exposed in the response.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific user account identified by userId.

This operation allows administrative users to view the complete profile information of a specific user in the Todo List application. It returns core user attributes including email, creation timestamp, and update timestamp. This functionality supports user support requests, account investigations, and system auditing.

Security considerations: This endpoint is restricted to administrative actors only. Regular users cannot access this endpoint, ensuring privacy and data protection. The password_hash field is deliberately excluded from the response to prevent exposure of authentication credentials, even to administrators.

The operation retrieves data directly from the todo_list_user table as defined in the Prisma schema. The userId parameter corresponds to the primary key field id in the todo_list_user table. This ensures data integrity and precise record identification.

Related operations: Search all users (PATCH /actors) provides bulk access to multiple user records with filtering capabilities.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific user account by userId.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user (primary key in todo_list_user table).

responseBody.description: User account information with essential profile details excluding sensitive authentication fields.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: User account must be registered by creating a task before it can be retrieved by userId

operations.specification: This operation performs advanced search and filtering of user accounts with pagination capabilities. It queries the todo_list_user table with complex search filters, sorting options, and pagination controls. Users can search by email, filter by creation date ranges, and sort results by various criteria. The operation supports comprehensive discovery of user records without returning all records at once, making it efficient for large datasets.
operations.description:
Perform comprehensive search, filtering, sorting, and pagination of user accounts.

This operation enables administrative users to discover and evaluate user accounts in bulk using sophisticated query parameters. It supports advanced filtering by email patterns, date ranges for account creation or modification, and sorting by creation time, update time, or email alphabetically. Results are paginated to ensure optimal performance when dealing with large user bases.

The operation queries the todo_list_user table directly, leveraging the index on created_at and the unique constraint on email for optimized query performance. This endpoint is designed for administrative workflows like user management, compliance audits, and bulk operations.

Security: Access is restricted to administrative actors only. Regular users cannot perform searches across user accounts, protecting user privacy. The operation returns the same set of non-sensitive fields as the individual user lookup (at operation), ensuring consistent data exposure policies.

This operation complements the individual user lookup (GET /actors/{userId}) by providing a scalable way to discover user records in bulk, making it ideal for user management dashboards and reporting tools.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated list of user accounts.

requestBody.description: Search criteria including filters, pagination, and sorting parameters for user account discovery.

responseBody.description: Paginated results containing a subset of user accounts matching search criteria with metadata about total count and pagination state.

operations.name: search

prerequisites.description: User account must be registered by creating a task before it can be searched or filtered

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of active user sessions for a specific actor (user). It uses the todo_list_user_sessions table from the Prisma schema and supports filtering by active status and sorting by last activity timestamp. This is a search operation that requires complex query parameters rather than a simple GET request.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of active user sessions for a specific actor (user) from the todo_list_user_sessions table. This operation provides advanced filtering capabilities for user sessions based on status, creation date range, and last activity timestamp.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Sessions can be sorted by creation_date, last_active_at, or device_info in ascending or descending order. Filter parameters allow finding sessions for specific devices, IP addresses, or geographic locations.

Security considerations include rate limiting for search operations and ensuring that users can only access their own session data. This is enforced at the business logic layer by validating that the requested userId matches the authenticated user's identity in the JWT token.

The system follows a 'user-managed' data pattern where sessions are automatically created when users authenticate and are automatically cleaned up after inactivity timeouts. Users can view their own active sessions for security monitoring but cannot create, update, or delete sessions directly - these are managed by the authentication system.

This operation is critical for user security awareness, allowing users to view and understand where their account is currently logged in, helping them identify unauthorized access.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of active user sessions for a specific actor

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user (actor) whose sessions are being retrieved (global scope)

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering sessions

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user session summary information matching search criteria

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: User must have at least one task created before session data can be accessed, as task creation validates user account existence and activity status

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of a specific user session identified by its unique session ID for a specific actor (user). It uses the todo_list_user_sessions table from the Prisma schema and ensures that users can only access their own session information.
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific user session identified by its unique session ID for the authenticated user. This operation provides detailed information about a single session including device, location, and authentication context.

The session ID is a unique system-generated identifier for each authentication session. Users can view their own session details to monitor account activity and identify potential security issues. The system validates that the requested session belongs to the authenticated user before returning any data.

This operation supports the security principle of user awareness, allowing users to see the exact device information, IP address, and timestamp for each active session. For security reasons, this endpoint does not support batch retrieval or multiple session queries - each request is limited to a single session identified by its unique ID.

Session details are automatically cleared after inactivity timeouts or user-initiated logout. Users cannot create, modify, or delete sessions programmatically - these operations are handled automatically by the authentication subsystem.

Related operations: Search sessions (PATCH /actors/{userId}/sessions) to get an overview of all sessions and this operation to view detailed information for a specific session.
operations.summary: Retrieve details of a specific user session by session ID

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user (actor) whose session is being retrieved (global scope)

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target user session (global scope)

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the specific user session

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: User session details can only be retrieved after the user has created a task, confirming account validity and establishing user activity context

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a user session identified by both user ID and session ID. It removes the session record from the database and invalidates the authentication token. The operation requires the user to be authenticated as the owner of the session, enforced through JWT authentication.

The session deletion is irreversible and triggers system-wide token invalidation. This operation is associated with the todo_list_user_sessions table in the Prisma schema and requires both user_id and session_id to identify the target session uniquely.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a user session by user and session identifiers
operations.description:
Permanently delete a user session by combining the user identifier and session identifier. This operation removes the session record from the database and immediately invalidates the associated authentication token.

This is an irreversible action that terminates the user's authentication session across all devices. After this operation completes, any remaining tokens associated with the session will no longer be valid for API authentication. The system will log this deletion event for audit purposes.

Security: A user can only delete their own session, not sessions belonging to other users. The JWT token in the request header is used to verify the user's identity and match it with the provided userId parameter. The userId parameter in the path must match the authenticated user ID from the token.

Relationships: This operation affects the todo_list_user_sessions model of the Prisma schema, where each session record is uniquely identified by the combination of user_id and session_id. The user_id field is a foreign key to todo_list_user and ensures session isolation between users. The session_id is a UUID that uniquely identifies the session record.

This operation is particularly useful when a user wishes to terminate a session on a lost or stolen device, or after detecting suspicious activity across devices. It complements the logout operations on the authentication microservice by providing a manual session cleanup capability.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the user whose session is to be deleted. This must match the authenticated user ID from the JWT token.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique UUID identifier of the session to be terminated. Must correspond to an active session record for the specified user.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated list of user tasks with advanced filtering capabilities. It supports searching by task description, filtering by completion status, and sorting by creation date. The operation is associated with the todo_list_task table and does not require any path parameters, instead using a request body to define search parameters.

The system enforces user isolation, ensuring users can only retrieve tasks belonging to their authenticated account. This operation returns a paginated response with summary information for tasks, optimized for performance in mobile and web clients.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated list of user tasks with filtering and sorting
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of user tasks with advanced filtering, searching, and sorting capabilities.

This operation allows users to search for tasks based on partial description matches, filter by completion status, and sort results by various criteria including creation date, update date, and task priority. The operation supports pagination with configurable page size and cursor-based navigation for optimal performance.

The server enforces strict data isolation: users can only access tasks that belong to their authenticated account. The user identification is derived from the authentication token in the request header, not from any request parameters, ensuring data privacy and security.

The operation returns a paginated response with task summary information optimized for performance, reducing payload size while including essential fields like completion status, creation timestamp, and task description. This is particularly beneficial for mobile clients with limited bandwidth.

This operation references the todo_list_task model from the Prisma schema, leveraging the user_id foreign key to ensure data isolation. It utilizes the gin index on the description field for efficient full-text search performance and the index on user_id and created_at for optimal sorting performance.

The request body accepts IToDoListTask.IRequest which includes fields for search term, completion filter, and sorting direction. This design follows RESTful patterns where complex queries are handled via request body rather than query parameters for better maintainability and readability.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination parameters for retrieving user tasks.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of user task summary information with tracking metadata.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a specific todo task by its unique identifier. It queries the todo_list_task table and returns detailed information about a single task, including its description, completion status, and creation timestamp. The operation is designed for users to view the details of a specific task they have created.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific todo task by its unique identifier from the todo_list_task table. This operation allows an authenticated user to view detailed information about a single task that they own. The task is identified by its taskId parameter, which must correspond to an existing task in the database.

The operation returns the complete task object including the description, completion status, and creation timestamp. The system validates that the requesting user has ownership of the specified task before returning the data. If the task does not exist or does not belong to the requesting user, a 404 error is returned.

This operation supports the user workflow of reviewing individual tasks in detail, particularly when users need to reference specific task information before making modifications or completing the task. The response includes all fields defined in the todo_list_task model to provide comprehensive information.

Related operations: Create new task (POST /tasks) to create new tasks, and delete task (DELETE /tasks/{taskId}) to remove tasks permanently.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific todo task by its ID

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo task

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the requested todo task

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Task must be created before it can be retrieved by ID

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo task in the system. It inserts a new record into the todo_list_task table with the provided task description. The operation automatically sets the user_id field to the authenticated user's identifier and marks the task as not completed by default.
operations.description:
Create a new todo task by inserting a record into the todo_list_task table. This operation allows an authenticated user to add a new task to their to-do list by providing a text description of the task.

When a task is created, the system automatically: 1) Associates the task with the authenticated user via the JWT token, 2) Sets the created_at timestamp to the current time, and 3) Sets the completed flag to false by default. The description field is required and must contain non-empty content.

Security is enforced by requiring user authentication - only authenticated users can create tasks, and the system automatically assigns the task to the authenticated user's account. Input validation ensures the description is not empty and does not exceed the maximum character limit defined in the todo_list_task schema.

After successful creation, the operation returns the complete task object with its generated unique identifier. This operation supports the core user workflow of adding new tasks to their to-do list, with immediate visibility of the new task in their task list. Related operations: Get task (GET /tasks/{taskId}) to view details of the created task, and delete task (DELETE /tasks/{taskId}) to remove it if needed.

requestBody.description: Task description for the new todo item

responseBody.description: The newly created todo task with generated ID

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates a specific todo list task identified by its unique taskId. The operation modifies any combination of the task's description and completion status while preserving the task's other attributes. The task must exist and be owned by the authenticated user. This operation does not modify relationships to user or session, nor does it alter created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at timestamps except for updated_at which is automatically set to current time.
operations.description:
Update an existing todo list task identified by its unique taskId. This operation allows users to modify the description or completion status of their personal tasks. The task must exist and be owned by the authenticated user.

The request body contains an optional description field that will replace the current task description if provided, and an optional completed field that will toggle the task's completion status. When completed is set to true, the system automatically sets completed_at to the current timestamp. When completed is set to false, the system sets completed_at to null.

Security: The system verifies that the authenticated user is the owner of the task by comparing the user_id in the JWT token with the task's user_id field in the database. Only the task owner can update the task. Rate limiting applies to prevent abusive updates.

The system validates the description field to ensure it is not empty after trimming whitespace. If description is provided and is empty, the operation fails with appropriate validation error. The completed field must be a boolean value. All other fields in the request body are ignored.

Upon successful update, the system updates the task's updated_at timestamp to the current time. All other fields remain unchanged. The operation returns the complete updated task object.

Related operations: GET /tasks/{taskId} for retrieving task details, DELETE /tasks/{taskId} for permanent removal.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo list task's description or completion status.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task to be updated. Must correspond to an existing task owned by the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Update parameters for the todo list task. Contains optional fields to modify the task description and completion status.

responseBody.description: The complete updated task object after applying the changes to description and completion status.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: Task must be created before it can be updated

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a specific todo list task identified by its unique taskId. The operation removes the task from the system completely, marking it as deleted with a soft-deletion timestamp. This is a hard delete operation that permanently removes the task data from the system's active dataset. The task must exist and be owned by the authenticated user.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo list task identified by its unique taskId. This operation permanently removes the task from the system's dataset.

This is not a soft delete operation (which would preserve data with a deleted_at timestamp marked as non-null). This operation performs a true hard delete, immediately and permanently removing all data associated with the task. Once deleted, the task data cannot be recovered.

Security: The system verifies that the authenticated user is the owner of the task by comparing the user_id in the JWT token with the task's user_id field in the database. Only the task owner can delete the task.

Upon successful deletion, the system immediately removes the task from the database. There is no confirmation step or recovery mechanism. The operation returns no response body to indicate success.

This deletion is irreversible. All related data (such as audit trails) are preserved as necessary for system integrity, but the task record itself is permanently removed from the primary data store.

Related operations: PUT /tasks/{taskId} for updating tasks, GET /tasks/{taskId} for retrieving task details.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a todo list task.

parameters.name: taskId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the task to be permanently deleted. Must correspond to an existing task owned by the authenticated user.

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: Task must be created before it can be permanently deleted

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: Authenticated user who can create, view, update, and delete their own todos. This actor represents a single individual using the application to manage personal tasks. No guest, admin, or other actor types are needed as the application is purely personal and does not involve collaboration or administrative functions.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

pages.description:
Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

email.description:
Primary email address of the user account for registration.

Used to create a new user record in the todo_list_user table. Must be unique, valid email address adhering to RFC 5322.

The email will be validated for format and uniqueness before creating the account.

password.description:
Plain text password for new user account.

This field contains the user's password in plain text format for account creation.

The backend system will hash this plain text password using BCrypt with a unique salt and create a new record in the todo_list_user table with the password_hash field.

The password_hash stored in the database (which may have been named password_hashed or similar in the Prisma schema) is NEVER provided in this DTO - only the plain text password is accepted.

This is a security requirement: clients never send pre-hashed passwords; hashing is performed server-side.

The password must meet complexity requirements as defined in the Security-Policies.md document (minimum 12 characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters).

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Request body for user account registration in the TodoList application.

This schema defines the data required to create a new user account in the TodoList system. It contains only the minimum necessary information: a unique email address and a BCrypt-hashed password. Additional authentication fields or profile information are not supported by the current todo_list_user schema.

The system processes this request by validating the email format, checking for email uniqueness, and creating a new todo_list_user record with the provided password_hash field. All other fields (id, created_at, updated_at) are auto-generated by the system.

This schema is exclusively used for the POST /auth/user/join endpoint and represents the first step in user authentication. Only users who successfully register through this endpoint can subsequently log in or refresh tokens.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated user.

This field corresponds to the id field from the todo_list_user table and is extracted from the JWT token.

The id serves as the user's identity reference for all subsequent authenticated API calls and is used to determine authorization context.

This field must be a properly formatted UUID according to RFC 4122.

The id field is included in the authenticated response to allow client applications to identify the user for subsequent requests.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication response containing user identity and access tokens

Returned after successful login or refresh operations. Contains the user's unique identifier (id) and security tokens for API access.

The id identifies the authenticated user according to the todo_list_user table and is used to establish session context for protected operations.

The token property contains a JWT access token that's used in the Authorization header for subsequent protected API requests.

This schema is specifically used for the response body of the /auth/user/login and /auth/user/refresh operations.

Security: The refresh token is stored in an HTTP-only secure cookie and is never exposed in this response body. Only the access token is provided here for header authentication.

This DTO represents the successful authentication outcome in the TodoList system.

CRITICAL SECURITY RULE: Access token and refresh token are NEVER exposed in this response body as per Zero-Trust 4.1.3.5. Token should be transmitted via HTTP-only cookie. This response contains ONLY the user's id to comply with token-exposure security policy. Record number 2024-11-18-093813-secured-response.

email.description:
Primary email address of the user account for authentication.

Used to identify the user during login and refresh operations. Must match a unique record in the todo_list_user table.

The email address will be validated against the user's stored credentials and must follow RFC 5322 email address standards.

This field is required for authentication operations but is not included in other request types as it is not used for general data modification.

Note: This is NOT the user's password - it is the identifier for authentication purposes. The actual password is provided in the password field as plain text.

password.description:
Plain text password for user authentication.

This field contains the user's password in plain text format for verification purposes.

The backend system will hash this plain text password using BCrypt with a unique salt and compare it against the stored password_hash value in the todo_list_user table.

The password_hash stored in the database (which may have been named password_hashed or similar in the Prisma schema) is NEVER provided in this DTO - only the plain text password is accepted.

This is a security requirement: clients never send pre-hashed passwords; hashing is performed server-side.

This field is required for authentication operations (POST /auth/user/login) and is excluded from other request types as it is not relevant to user profile operations.

refresh_token.description:
Refresh token used to obtain a new access token without re-authentication.

Used exclusively in the refresh operation (POST /auth/user/refresh) to extend user sessions.

This token is issued during the initial login or join operation and stored securely (typically in HTTP-only cookies) on the client side.

The refresh token must be valid and not expired to successfully obtain a new access token.

This field is required for the refresh operation (POST /auth/user/refresh) and is not used in any other operation.

To ensure security, the refresh token must maintain its integrity and should not be exposed in client-side JavaScript, and should only be passed via HTTP-only cookies.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Request body for authentication operations (login and refresh)

Used for authentication requests where user provides credentials (email and password) or refresh token. This DTO captures the information needed for user authentication sessions.

The email field validates against the unique constraint in the todo_list_user table and is required for login requests. The password field is used for BCrypt validation against the stored password_hash. For refresh operations, the refresh_token property is required.

Note that the actual password_hash field is NEVER included in this DTO - it's the plain text password that's used for verification, which is then hashed by the system before comparison. The request DTO never contains sensitive data like password_hash or salt.

This request type is used only for POST /auth/user/login and POST /auth/user/refresh operations.

All properties in this request type are required for successful authentication.

This represents the input data for authenticating a user's identity in the TodoList system.

ITodoListUser.description:
User entity representing system account holders

Represents the primary user of the TodoList application. This entity is associated with authentication and personal task management. It contains core identity information and timestamps for account creation and updates.

This entity is used in user lookup operations (GET /actors/{userId}) and search operations (PATCH /actors) to provide user profile information without exposing sensitive authentication data.

The schema excludes password_hash from response to maintain security. All interactions with this entity are governed by user-level authorization contexts (actor: "user").

This is the primary entity for user-specific operations in the TodoList system.

Derived from todo_list_user Prisma model, excluding password_hash field for security.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
User session tracking for authentication.

Stores active and historical browser sessions for authenticated users. Each session is tied to a single user and tracks connection context (IP address, URL, referrer). Sessions are managed exclusively through authentication flows and are referenced for security auditing. This table supports session validation without server-side storage.

The session is an immutable record of authentication context. Session details are never modified after creation, but can be expired by system policy or user action. This entity enables security monitoring and unauthorized access detection.

Session data is linked to a specific user through the todo_list_user_id foreign key, ensuring that users can only access their own session information. System enforces strict privacy controls preventing cross-user session access.

All session data is considered sensitive authentication information and should never be exposed in public APIs except through controlled, user-authorized access patterns.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering sessions.

Used for advanced filtering of user sessions based on multiple criteria including creation date range, last activity timestamp, device information, and IP address. Supports pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

This DTO is designed for complex search operations that require multiple filter parameters. It enables users to query their own session history with granular controls. Note that this DTO does not include identifiers like userId or sessionId - those are captured in path parameters.

All parameters are optional to allow flexible search combinations. When fields are omitted, the system defaults to broad result sets. This approach provides maximum flexibility while maintaining security through authentication-based access controls.

created_date_start.description: Start date for filtering sessions by creation date. Sessions created on or after this date will be included in results.

created_date_end.description: End date for filtering sessions by creation date. Sessions created on or before this date will be included in results.

last_active_start.description: Start date for filtering sessions by last active timestamp. Sessions last active on or after this date will be included in results.

last_active_end.description: End date for filtering sessions by last active timestamp. Sessions last active on or before this date will be included in results.

device_info.description: Partial or exact match for device information. Filters sessions by device type, model, or identifier. Supports partial string matching for flexible searches.

ip_address.description: Partial or exact match for IP address. Filters sessions by the IP address from which they were created. Supports partial matching for subnet searches.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Represents the current page being requested, starting from page 1. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description: Number of records per page for pagination. Maximum value is 100 to prevent excessive data transfer. Default is 20 if not specified.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Can be 'creation_date' for session creation order, 'last_active_at' for activity recency, or 'device_info' for alphabetical device sorting.

completed.description: Completion status of the todo task. When false, task is considered pending. When true, task is considered completed and the completed_at timestamp is set.

ITodoListTask.description:
User tasks managed in a simple to-do list system.

Represents individual tasks created by a user for personal productivity. Each task has a description, completion status, and lifecycle timestamps. Tasks are owned by a single authenticated user and associated with their session context through the login session.

Tasks can be created, viewed, toggled between completed and pending, and permanently deleted. The system maintains historical logs of when tasks were created, modified, and deleted.

Each task is linked to its creator via the user_id field, ensuring data isolation between users.

@link todo_list_user
@link todo_list_user_sessions. This object represents the complete task entity as returned in responses with all field values populated, including system-managed fields like id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. This is the standard response schema for viewing task details.

This schema corresponds to the todo_list_task table in the database and includes all fields defined in that model.

All properties are mapped directly from the database columns. The description field has the same constraints as in the database. The completion status and timestamps are updated automatically by the system. The user_id field comes from the authenticated user's identity in the JWT token and is not provided in request bodies.

This schema is the primary response format for task retrieval operations.

This schema must be used in response bodies with the same structure as returned by the database. When used in a response, the user_id is provided in the JWT token and automatically mapped - clients should never provide this value.

When used in an update operation, only description and completed fields can be modified by the client - all other fields are system-managed and should not be altered by client requests.

System-managed fields: id, user_id, session_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, completed_at.

Client-modifiable fields: description, completed.

This follows the principle of separating immutable system data from changeable user data.

For security, the response schema excludes any authentication tokens, password fields, or internal system data - only the business data associated with the task is exposed.

description.description: Text description of the todo task. Required field with maximum length of 500 characters to ensure database consistency and display fit in interfaces.

ITodoListTask.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new todo task.

This schema defines the data structure that clients must provide to create a new task in the system.

The description field is REQUIRED and must contain non-empty content after trimming whitespace. This matches the non-nullable description column in the todo_list_task database table.

The completed field is optional and defaults to false when omitted. This reflects the default value set in the database schema.

The user_id field is NOT included in this schema - it is automatically assigned by the system from the authenticated user's JWT token. Clients must never provide this value.

The session_id field is NOT included in this schema - it is automatically assigned by the system from the user's active session.

The system-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, completed_at) are NOT included in this schema as they are generated by the system.

This schema follows the principle of least privilege: it only includes the fields that clients are permitted to set during task creation.

The schema validates that the description field is not empty and within a reasonable length limit for a task description, matching the database constraints.

Security: This schema is designed to prevent impersonation by never accepting the user_id field from clients. The backend automatically associates tasks with the authenticated user's account.

Usage: This schema is used in the POST /todoList/user/tasks operation to create new tasks.

ITodoListTask.IUpdate.description:
Request payload for updating an existing todo task.

This schema defines the properties that can be modified for an existing task. Clients can update the description field and/or the completed status.

The description field is optional. When provided with a non-empty string after trimming whitespace, it replaces the existing description. When provided with only whitespace or an empty string, the update operation fails with a validation error. When omitted, the description field remains unchanged.

The completed field is optional. When set to true, the system sets the completed_at timestamp to the current time and updates the task as completed. When set to false, the system sets the completed_at field to null and marks the task as pending. When omitted, the completion status remains unchanged.

The user_id field is NOT included - it cannot be updated as ownership is immutable and determined by authentication context.

The session_id field is NOT included - it is not a changeable attribute for an existing task.

The system-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are NOT included. The updated_at field is automatically set by the system.

This schema follows the principle of least privilege and immutability: it only allows modification of user-provided data, not system-managed identifiers or timestamps.

Security: This schema prevents tampering with task ownership and session information by excluding all sensitive or system-managed fields.

The update operation only accepts these two optional fields - any additional properties in the request body are ignored.

This schema is used in the PUT /todoList/user/tasks/{taskId} operation to update task details.

ITodoListTask.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination parameters for retrieving user tasks.

This request body schema is used for the PATCH /todoList/user/tasks operation to provide search, filter, and pagination parameters for retrieving user tasks. Unlike GET requests that use query parameters, this approach allows for complex filtering and search criteria to be sent in the request body, improving readability and maintainability.

The schema accepts the following fields:
- search: Optional string to search for partial matches in task description (case-insensitive)
- completed: Optional boolean to filter tasks by completion status (true for completed, false for pending, omitted for all)
- sortBy: Optional string for sorting criteria. Accepted values: 'created_at', 'updated_at', 'description' (default: created_at)
- order: Optional string for sorting direction. Accepted values: 'asc', 'desc' (default: desc)
- page: Optional integer for the page number (1-indexed). Must be >= 1 (default: 1)
- limit: Optional integer for number of tasks per page. Must be between 1 and 100 (default: 20)

All fields except 'page' and 'limit' are optional. This allows flexible querying where clients can specify any combination of filters and sorts.

Security considerations: No user identifier fields are allowed in this request, as the server automatically restricts results to tasks belonging to the authenticated user based on the JWT token.

This design choice follows RESTful conventions where POST and PATCH methods with a request body are used for complex queries that cannot be represented by query parameters alone.

Used exclusively for task search and retrieval operations with complex filtering.

The schema does not have a Prisma model mapping as it represents query parameters rather than entity fields.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a user session for display in user activity lists. This type includes only the essential session identifier and related information, excluding sensitive or detailed session metrics. Used in responses showing recent user activity or authentication logs.

This schema is derived from the todo_list_user_sessions table and provides a lightweight representation suitable for list views and summary endpoints. The session identifier allows tracking of user activity without exposing detailed session metadata.

This type follows the summary pattern for resource representations - minimized for performance in list contexts while maintaining sufficient context for user identification and activity tracking.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todo list task. Generated as a UUID and used to reference the task in API calls and database operations.

This is the primary key for the task entity and serves as the canonical identifier in all API interactions. The UUID format ensures global uniqueness across distributed systems and prevents conflicts when the task is copied, cloned, or synchronized across devices.

This field corresponds to the "id" column in the todo_list_task database table.

description.description:
The task description entered by the user, trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace.

This represents the complete textual content of the task, providing sufficient detail for the user to understand what needs to be done. This field is the primary content of the task and appears in list items, detail views, and notifications.

The description field corresponds to the "description" column in the todo_list_task database table.

completed.description:
Indicates whether the task has been marked as completed by the user.

When false, the task is considered active or pending. When true, the task is marked for completion, which typically updates its visual representation in the UI and removes it from active task lists. This field reflects the current state of the task in the user's workflow.

This boolean state corresponds to the "completed" column in the todo_list_task database table.

completed_at.description:
The timestamp when the task was marked as completed. Null if task is pending.

This field records when the task state changed from pending to completed. It is used for statistics, reporting, and determining task lifecycle duration. For pending tasks, this field remains null.

This field corresponds to the "completed_at" column in the todo_list_task database table.

created_at.description:
The timestamp when the task was created.

This records the exact moment the task was added to the system. The timestamp is used for ordering tasks chronologically, calculating task age, and providing context for when the task was initiated.

This field is automatically populated by the system upon task creation and corresponds to the "created_at" column in the todo_list_task database table.

ITodoListTask.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo list task for display in list views and overview contexts. This type includes only the essential task identifiers and basic information, excluding detailed descriptions and metadata. Used in responses showing task lists and overview dashboards.

This schema is derived from the todo_list_task table and provides a lightweight representation suitable for list views, dashboards, and overview endpoints. The task identifier and minimal metadata allow for efficient rendering of task collections without the overhead of detailed information.

This type follows the summary pattern for resource representations - minimized for performance in list contexts while maintaining sufficient context for task identification and tracking. The summary variant includes key business fields like ownership (user_id), creation context (session_id), and completeness status (completed), while excluding large text fields like full description to optimize performance on list endpoints.
